human.problem: Two different Antiochs appear. Stop 1 card 1 names 'Pisidian Antioch', and stop 3 card 4 says they return to 'Antioch' (Acts 14:21, Pisidian Antioch). Stop 3 card 11 then says they sail to 'Antioch, where this whole journey started' (Acts 14:26, the Antioch of Acts 13:1-3), followed by 'Full circle, friend.' A baker may think this is the same city they just returned to in card 4.
human.question: When a passage names two different places with the same name, should Papa Dorin say which one is meant each time it comes up (for example, 'Pisidian Antioch' on stop 3 card 4, and 'the Antioch they started from' on card 11)?
